source.title: LYSAGHT Zeds and Cees Design and Installation Guide
pages: 13: PB1230HS M12 x 30 grade 8.8 purlin-bolt catalogue identity
17-18: Cee holes, 100AC cleats, orientation and bridging locations

references: AS/NZS 4600:2005 incorporating Amendment No. 1, clauses 4.3.2.1-4.3.2.3 and 5.3; SHA-256 9af589ce2bfee5a156c7f6600a738fcc158683bd27bea9d22adb559f172fc2d1

resistance.basis: The exact C10012, 100AC and two PB1230HS purlin-web bolt kits establish a physically capable lateral/twist-restraint candidate. Tertius calculates the 2.5% critical-flange force required by AS/NZS 4600:2005 clauses 4.3.2.2-4.3.2.3. Capacity and stiffness remain unverified because the rendered physical joint does not yet include the separate support-side shared bolts that connect the 100AC leg to the C10019 rafter.

assumptions: C10012 is a single-span secondary member between portal frames.
Each rendered purlin-web fastener is one PB1230HS M12 x 30 grade 8.8 bolt/nut/washer kit.
The 100AC-to-rafter support-side bolt group must be included in the same physical connection before resistance or stiffness can be credited.
A separate longitudinal roof-bracing or verified diaphragm path is required.
exclusions: No connection stiffness is inferred from bracket geometry.
No support-side bolt resistance is inferred from unlinked nearby geometry.
No rafter distortional-buckling resistance is inferred from purlin load tables.
No cladding-diaphragm capacity or collector anchorage is credited.

resistance.basis: The exact C10012, 100AC, 100CP and two PB1230HS purlin-web bolt kits establish a physically capable lateral/twist-restraint candidate at the open rafter face. Tertius calculates the AS/NZS 4600:2005 2.5% critical-flange force, but cannot credit resistance or stiffness until the shared support-side bolt group is part of this physical connection identity.

assumptions: C10012 is a single-span secondary member between portal frames.
Each rendered purlin-web fastener is one PB1230HS M12 x 30 grade 8.8 bolt/nut/washer kit.
The 100CP is a rendered clamp plate and is not a substitute for the missing support-side bolt identity.
exclusions: No connection stiffness is inferred from bracket or clamp-plate geometry.
No support-side bolt resistance is inferred from unlinked nearby geometry.
No cladding-diaphragm or collector anchorage is credited.

packs.label: C10012 full-depth solid bridge / 100AC / PB1230HS candidate

source.title: LYSAGHT Zeds and Cees Design and Installation Guide
pages: 9: solid bridging secured to purlin webs resists tension, compression and bending and controls lateral deflection and twist
13: PB1230HS M12 x 30 grade 8.8 purlin-bolt catalogue identity and 100AC catalogue geometry
17-18: Cee bridging holes, cleat holes and M12 hole geometry

references: AS/NZS 4600:2005 incorporating Amendment No. 1, clauses 4.3.2.1-4.3.2.3 and 5.3; SHA-256 9af589ce2bfee5a156c7f6600a738fcc158683bd27bea9d22adb559f172fc2d1

resistance.basis: The exact rendered C10012 full-depth bridge, one 100AC angle and four PB1230HS bolts establish a two-sided web restraint candidate. The manufacturer guide verifies the solid-bridging mechanism, but publishes system capacities for approved HOOK-LOK II end hardware rather than this substituted 100AC joint. A project connection calculation or test is still required before resistance and stiffness can be credited.

assumptions: The bridge Cee web lies parallel to the roof plane and spans between adjacent purlin webs.
Two PB1230HS bolts connect the 100AC to the bridge web and two separate PB1230HS bolts connect its support leg to the purlin web.
The four bolts and 100AC are registered in one physical connection identity.
The continuous bridging run is connected into a separately verified longitudinal roof-bracing path.
exclusions: The LYSAGHT capacity tables do not verify a 100AC substitution for HOOK-LOK II end hardware.
No bracket rotational stiffness or plate resistance is inferred from rendered geometry.
No longitudinal anchorage is inferred from topology alone.
